chain.label: Night conditions with unlit runway 26
chain.trigger: Night visual meteorological conditions (VMC) prevailed at the time of the accident; runway 26 had no lighting

chain.label: FAA regulation allowed runway crossings without specific ATC clearance
chain.trigger: 14 CFR 91.129(i) permits pilots instructed to taxi to a point on the airport surface to cross all intersecting runways along the taxi route (without stopping) except for the assigned departure runway

chain.label: Captain gave abbreviated taxi briefing, omitting the runway 26 crossing
chain.trigger: the captain stated, “Comair standard,”" instead of the full required briefing on the crew's first flight together

chain.label: Flight crew held nonpertinent conversation during taxi (sterile cockpit violation)
chain.trigger: the flight crew engaged in conversation that was not pertinent to the operation of the flight

caused_by.evidence: the captain's abbreviated taxi briefing and both pilots' nonpertinent conversation, most likely created an atmosphere in the cockpit that enabled the crew's errors

chain.label: Flight crew lost positional awareness on the airport surface during taxi
chain.trigger: the flight crewmembers' nonpertinent conversation during taxi ... likely contributed to their loss of positional awareness

caused_by.evidence: nonpertinent conversation during taxi, which resulted in a loss of positional awareness

chain.label: Crew taxied onto and lined up for takeoff on runway 26 instead of assigned runway 22
chain.trigger: the captain and the first officer believed that the airplane was on runway 22 when they taxied onto runway 26 and initiated the takeoff roll

caused_by.evidence: runway 26 had no lighting, unlike the illuminated runway 22 environment the crew expected

chain.label: Crew failed to cross-check aircraft position/heading before takeoff despite contradictory cues
chain.trigger: the flight crewmembers failed to recognize that they were initiating a takeoff on the wrong runway because they did not cross-check and confirm the airplane's position on the runway before takeoff and they were likely influenced by confirmation bias

caused_by.evidence: once the flight crewmembers had navigated to what they believed was the correct runway, they were likely no longer giving strong weight to contradictory information as a result of confirmation bias

chain.label: Controller performed an administrative traffic count instead of monitoring the departure
chain.trigger: instead of monitoring the airplane's departure, he performed a lower-priority administrative task [the traffic count] that could have waited until he transferred responsibility for the airplane

caused_by.evidence: if these safety recommendations had been implemented ... the controller would have been required to ... visually observe the airplane's position and monitor the taxi

chain.label: Crew recognized the wrong-runway takeoff too late to abort safely
chain.trigger: the flight crew recognized that something was wrong with the takeoff beyond the point from which the airplane could be stopped on the remaining available runway

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew had not correctly interpreted these cues or noticed them until after it was too late to successfully abort the takeoff
the controller missed his final opportunity to notice the flight crew's error in enough time to take action to prevent the accident

chain.label: Airplane ran off the end of runway 26
chain.trigger: The airplane ran off the end of the runway

caused_by.evidence: airplane accelerated beyond the maximum airspeed that would have allowed the airplane to remain on the available runway

chain.label: Airplane impacted berm, perimeter fence, and trees
chain.trigger: impacted the airport perimeter fence, trees, and terrain

caused_by.evidence: the airplane became temporarily airborne after impacting the berm ... impacted a tree located about 900 feet from the end of runway 26

chain.label: 49 fatalities and 1 serious injury; airplane destroyed by impact and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: The captain, flight attendant, and 47 passengers were killed, and the first officer received serious injuries. The airplane was destroyed by impact forces and postcrash fire.

caused_by.evidence: the fuselage traveled another 150 feet before coming to a stop. The airplane structure continued to burn
